metadata.title: Database-friendly Random Projections: Johnson-Lindenstrauss with Binary Coins
metadata.source_note: Extracted from PDF->text fallback; .tex source not available. Math fidelity reduced.

nodes.name: JL-embedding
nodes.statement: A map $f : \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}^k$ such that for all $u, v \in P$, $(1-\epsilon)\|u-v\|^2 \le \|f(u)-f(v)\|^2 \le (1+\epsilon)\|u-v\|^2$.
nodes.statement_clean: A map providing the distance-preservation guarantee of the Johnson-Lindenstrauss lemma.

nodes.name: Random projection matrix $R$
nodes.statement: A $d \times k$ random matrix $R$ with $R(i,j) = r_{ij}$, where $\{r_{ij}\}$ are independent random variables drawn from one of two specified discrete distributions on $\{-1,+1\}$ or $\{-\sqrt{3}, 0, +\sqrt{3}\}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Random projection matrix whose entries follow simple discrete distributions with mean 0 and variance 1.

nodes.name: Embedding map $f$ via $R$
nodes.statement: Let $E = \frac{1}{\sqrt{k}} A R$ and let $f : \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}^k$ map the $i$-th row of $A$ to the $i$-th row of $E$.
nodes.statement_clean: Definition of embedding via matrix multiplication with the random matrix $R$.

nodes.name: Worst-case unit vector $w$
nodes.statement: $w = \frac{1}{\sqrt{d}}(1, \ldots, 1)$, the all-ones unit vector in $\mathbb{R}^d$.
nodes.statement_clean: The all-ones unit vector identified as the worst-case input for concentration bounds.

nodes.name: Johnson-Lindenstrauss Lemma (cited)
nodes.statement: Given $\epsilon > 0$ and integer $n$, let $k_0 = O(\epsilon^{-2} \log n)$. For every set $P$ of $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^d$ there exists $f : \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}^k$ such that for all $u,v \in P$: $(1-\epsilon)\|u-v\|^2 \le \|f(u)-f(v)\|^2 \le (1+\epsilon)\|u-v\|^2$.
conclusions: There exists $f : \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}^k$ preserving all pairwise distances within factor $(1\pm\epsilon)$

nodes.name: Main Theorem (Theorem 2)
nodes.statement: Let $P$ be $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^d$, represented as $A$. Given $\epsilon, \beta > 0$, let $k_0 = \frac{4 + 2\beta}{\epsilon^2/2 - \epsilon^3/3}\log n$. With probability at least $1 - n^{-\beta}$, for all $u,v \in P$: $(1-\epsilon)\|u-v\|^2 \le \|f(u)-f(v)\|^2 \le (1+\epsilon)\|u-v\|^2$.
assumptions: $R$ uses one of the two distributions in the theorem
conclusions: With probability $\ge 1 - n^{-\beta}$, $f$ preserves pairwise squared distances within factor $(1\pm\epsilon)$

nodes.name: Frankl-Maehara Bound (Theorem 3, cited)
nodes.statement: For any $\epsilon \in (0, 1/2)$, any sufficiently large $P \subset \mathbb{R}^d$, and $k \ge k_0 = \lceil 9(\epsilon^2 - 2\epsilon^3/3)^{-1} \log |P| \rceil + 1$, there exists $f : P \to \mathbb{R}^k$ such that for all $u,v \in P$: $(1-\epsilon)\|u-v\|^2 \le \|f(u)-f(v)\|^2 \le (1+\epsilon)\|u-v\|^2$.
conclusions: There exists $f : P \to \mathbb{R}^k$ preserving pairwise squared distances within factor $(1\pm\epsilon)$

nodes.name: Spherical concentration (Lemma 4)
nodes.statement: Let $r_{ij} \stackrel{D}{=} N(0,1)$ for all $i,j$. Then for any $\epsilon > 0$ and any unit vector $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}^d$: $\Pr[\|f(\alpha)\|^2 \ge (1+\epsilon) k/d] < \exp(-k(\epsilon^2/2 - \epsilon^3/3)/2)$ and similarly for the lower tail.
conclusions: Both upper and lower tail probabilities of $\|f(\alpha)\|^2$ are bounded by $\exp(-k(\epsilon^2/2 - \epsilon^3/3)/2)$

nodes.name: Discrete concentration (Lemma 5)
nodes.statement: Let $r_{ij}$ have either of the two distributions in Theorem 2. Then for any $\epsilon > 0$ and any unit vector $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}^d$: $\Pr[S > (1+\epsilon)k/d] < \exp(-k(\epsilon^2/2 - \epsilon^3/3)/2)$ and $\Pr[S < (1-\epsilon)k/d] < \exp(-k(\epsilon^2/2 - \epsilon^3/3)/2)$.
assumptions: $r_{ij}$ from one of the two distributions in Theorem 2
conclusions: Both tail probabilities of $S$ are bounded by $\exp(-k(\epsilon^2/2 - \epsilon^3/3)/2)$

nodes.name: Moment bounds (Lemma 6)
nodes.statement: For all $h \in [0, d/2)$ and all $d \ge 1$: $\mathbb{E}[\exp(h Q_1^2)] \le 1/\sqrt{1 - 2h/d}$, and $\mathbb{E}[Q_1^4] \le 3/d^2$.

nodes.name: Worst-case vector dominates (Lemma 7)
nodes.statement: Let $w = (1/\sqrt{d})(1, \ldots, 1)$. For every unit vector $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}^d$ and all $k = 0, 1, \ldots$: $\mathbb{E}[Q(\alpha)^{2k}] \le \mathbb{E}[Q(w)^{2k}]$.
assumptions: $r_{ij}$ from one of the two distributions

nodes.name: Domination by Normal moments (Lemma 8)
nodes.statement: Let $T \stackrel{D}{=} N(0, 1/d)$. For all $d \ge 1$ and all $k = 0, 1, \ldots$: $\mathbb{E}[Q(w)^{2k}] \le \mathbb{E}[T^{2k}]$.
conclusions: The even moments of $Q(w)$ are dominated by those of the scaled Normal $T$

nodes.name: Pairwise moment swap (Lemma 9)
nodes.statement: Let $r_1, r_2$ be i.i.d. r.v. with one of the two distributions. For real $a, b$ let $\gamma = \sqrt{(a^2+b^2)/2}$. Then for all $T$ and $k = 0, 1, \ldots$: $\mathbb{E}[(T + a r_1 + b r_2)^{2k}] \le \mathbb{E}[(T + \gamma r_1 + \gamma r_2)^{2k}]$.
assumptions: $r_1, r_2$ i.i.d. from one of the two distributions
conclusions: Symmetrising weights $a, b$ to equal $\gamma$ does not decrease the even moments

nodes.name: Expected squared embedded length
nodes.statement: $\mathbb{E}[Q_j^2] = \frac{1}{d} \|\alpha\|^2$, hence $\mathbb{E}[\|f(\alpha)\|^2] = \|\alpha\|^2$.
nodes.statement_clean: The embedding $f$ preserves squared norms in expectation when $\mathbb{E}(r_{ij})=0$ and $\mathrm{Var}(r_{ij})=1$.

nodes.name: JL probability target inequality
nodes.statement: If $\Pr[(1-\epsilon)\|\alpha\|^2 \le \|f(\alpha)\|^2 \le (1+\epsilon)\|\alpha\|^2] \ge 1 - 2/n^{2+\beta}$ for every $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}^d$, then by union bound the failure probability is below $1/n^{\beta}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Per-vector concentration combined with union bound over pairs yields the JL guarantee.

nodes.name: Database-friendly random projection (sign / sparse-sign embedding)
nodes.statement: Generate $k$ new attributes by random sign sums (or sparse $\{-\sqrt{3}, 0, +\sqrt{3}\}$ sums) over the $d$ original attributes, then scale by $1/\sqrt{k}$.
input: Choice of distribution: $r_{ij} \in \{-1,+1\}$ uniform, or $r_{ij} \in \{-\sqrt{3}, 0, +\sqrt{3}\}$ with probabilities $1/6, 2/3, 1/6$
output: $n \times k$ embedded matrix $E = \frac{1}{\sqrt{k}} A R$ approximating Euclidean distances of $A$
nodes.pseudocode: 1. Sample $d \times k$ matrix $R$ with i.i.d. entries from chosen distribution. 2. Compute $E = (1/\sqrt{k}) A R$ via aggregations. 3. Each column of $R$ partitions attributes; for the sparse case, drop $2/3$ of attributes, randomly split the rest into two halves, sum each half, take their difference.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5
nodes.statement: Apply Markov's inequality to the moment generating function of $S$, factor over independent columns, then substitute Lemma 6 bounds and optimize over $h$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 6
nodes.statement: Compare term-by-term moments of $Q$ to those of $T \sim N(0, 1/d)$ via Lemmata 7 and 8; then use the Monotone Convergence Theorem to extend to $\mathbb{E}[\exp(h Q^2)]$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 7
nodes.statement: Show that for any unit $\alpha$ with $\alpha_1^2 \ne \alpha_2^2$, replacing $(\alpha_1, \alpha_2)$ by $(\gamma, \gamma)$ with $\gamma = \sqrt{(\alpha_1^2+\alpha_2^2)/2}$ does not decrease $\mathbb{E}[Q(\alpha)^{2k}]$ (using Lemma 9). Iterate to reach $w$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 8
nodes.statement: Express $T$ as a scaled sum of $d$ i.i.d. standard Normals. Compare term-by-term against $Q = (1/d) \sum Y_i$ using $\mathbb{E}[Y_1^{2\ell}] \le \mathbb{E}[T_1^{2\ell}] = (2\ell-1)!!$ for both candidate distributions.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 9
nodes.statement: Expand $\mathbb{E}[(T + \gamma r_1 + \gamma r_2)^{2k}] - \mathbb{E}[(T + a r_1 + b r_2)^{2k}] = S_k / 4$ via the binomial theorem; show all terms $D_{2j} \ge 0$ using $(x+y)^j \ge x^j + y^j$ for $x, y \ge 0$.

nodes.name: Markov on MGF
nodes.statement: For $h > 0$: $\Pr[S > (1+\epsilon)k/d] = \Pr[\exp(hS) > \exp(h(1+\epsilon)k/d)] < \mathbb{E}[\exp(hS)] \exp(-h(1+\epsilon)k/d)$.

nodes.name: Factor MGF over independent columns
nodes.statement: $\mathbb{E}[\exp(hS)] = \prod_{j=1}^k \mathbb{E}[\exp(h Q_j^2)] = (\mathbb{E}[\exp(h Q_1^2)])^k$ by independence and identical distribution.

nodes.name: Substitute Lemma 6 MGF bound
nodes.statement: Substitute $\mathbb{E}[\exp(h Q_1^2)] \le 1/\sqrt{1 - 2h/d}$ from Lemma 6 to obtain (13).

nodes.name: Optimize $h$ for upper tail
nodes.statement: Set the derivative w.r.t. $h$ to zero, giving $h = \frac{d}{2} \frac{\epsilon}{1+\epsilon} < d/2$. Substituting yields $((1+\epsilon)\exp(-\epsilon))^{k/2}$, then series expansion gives $\exp(-k(\epsilon^2/2 - \epsilon^3/3)/2)$.

nodes.name: Lower tail via expansion of $\exp(-h Q_1^2)$
nodes.statement: For lower tail, expand $\exp(-hQ_1^2) \le 1 - hQ_1^2 + (hQ_1^2)^2/2$, then use $\mathbb{E}[Q_1^2] = 1/d$ and $\mathbb{E}[Q_1^4] \le 3/d^2$ from Lemma 6 to get the analogous bound.

nodes.name: MCT and term-by-term comparison
nodes.statement: By the Monotone Convergence Theorem, $\mathbb{E}[\exp(h U^2)] = \sum_k h^k \mathbb{E}[U^{2k}] / k!$ for both $U = T$ and $U = Q$.

nodes.name: Apply Lemmata 7 and 8 termwise
nodes.statement: Use $\mathbb{E}[Q^{2k}] \le \mathbb{E}[Q(w)^{2k}] \le \mathbb{E}[T^{2k}]$ for each $k$ to bound $\mathbb{E}[\exp(h Q^2)] \le \mathbb{E}[\exp(h T^2)] = 1/\sqrt{1 - 2h/d}$.

nodes.name: Bound on $\mathbb{E}[Q^4]$
nodes.statement: Compute $\mathbb{E}[T^4] = 3/d^2$ directly from the Normal density and apply (19),(20) to obtain $\mathbb{E}[Q^4] \le 3/d^2$.

nodes.name: Reduce to balanced pair
nodes.statement: If $\alpha_1^2 = \alpha_2^2 = \cdots = \alpha_d^2$ then $\alpha = \pm w$ and the lemma is trivial; else assume $\alpha_1^2 \ne \alpha_2^2$ and define a more balanced unit vector $\alpha' = (\gamma, \gamma, \alpha_3, \ldots, \alpha_d)$.

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 9
nodes.statement: Express $\mathbb{E}[Q(\alpha)^{2k}]$ as an average over $r_{11}, r_{21}$, and apply Lemma 9 conditionally to obtain $\mathbb{E}[Q(\alpha)^{2k}] \le \mathbb{E}[Q(\alpha')^{2k}]$.

nodes.name: Iterate to reach $w$
nodes.statement: Apply the balancing step repeatedly across coordinate pairs; in the limit $\alpha$ becomes $w$, yielding $\mathbb{E}[Q(\alpha)^{2k}] \le \mathbb{E}[Q(w)^{2k}]$.

nodes.name: Express $T$ as scaled sum of i.i.d. Normals
nodes.statement: If $\{T_i\}_{i=1}^d$ are i.i.d. $N(0,1)$ then $\sum_i T_i \sim N(0,d)$, hence $T \stackrel{D}{=} (1/d) \sum_{i=1}^d T_i$, parallel in form to $Q(w) = (1/d) \sum_i Y_i$.

nodes.name: Termwise comparison of multinomial expansions
nodes.statement: Expand both expectations as $d^{-2k} \sum_{i_1, \ldots, i_{2k}} \mathbb{E}[\cdot]$. Reduce to single-coordinate moment comparison $\mathbb{E}[Y_1^{2\ell}] \le \mathbb{E}[T_1^{2\ell}]$.

nodes.name: Single-coordinate moment bound
nodes.statement: Use $\mathbb{E}[T_1^{2\ell}] = (2\ell-1)!! = (2\ell)!/(\ell! 2^\ell) \ge 1$. For $Y_1 \in \{\pm 1\}$, $\mathbb{E}[Y_1^{2\ell}] = 1$. For $Y_1 \in \{-\sqrt{3}, 0, \sqrt{3}\}$, $\mathbb{E}[Y_1^{2\ell}] = 3^{\ell-1} \le (2\ell)!/(\ell! 2^\ell)$ by induction.

nodes.name: Set-up sign case
nodes.statement: Consider $r_i \in \{-1,+1\}$ uniform; if $a^2 = b^2$ the lemma is trivial; else expand $\mathbb{E}[(T+\gamma r_1+\gamma r_2)^{2k}] - \mathbb{E}[(T+ar_1+br_2)^{2k}] = S_k/4$.

nodes.name: Binomial expansion of $S_k$
nodes.statement: Expand all $(T \pm \cdot)^{2k}$ via the binomial theorem; obtain $S_k = 2T^{2k} + \sum_{i=0}^{2k} \binom{2k}{i} T^{2k-i} D_i$ where $D_i = (2\gamma)^i + (-2\gamma)^i - (a+b)^i - (a-b)^i - (-a+b)^i - (-a-b)^i$.

nodes.name: Show $D_{2j} \ge 0$
nodes.statement: For odd $i$, $D_i = 0$. For even $i = 2j$, use $(2a^2+2b^2) = (a+b)^2 + (a-b)^2$ and $(x+y)^j \ge x^j + y^j$ for $x,y \ge 0$ to conclude $D_{2j} \ge 0$.

nodes.name: Sparse sign case
nodes.statement: The case $r_i \in \{-\sqrt{3}, 0, \sqrt{3}\}$ proceeds analogously but with more cumbersome enumeration; it is omitted in the main text. The threshold $2/3$ on $\Pr[r_i = 0]$ is tight for the lemma to hold.

nodes.name: Tightness of $2/3$ zero probability
nodes.statement: If one tries to take $r_i = 0$ with probability greater than $2/3$ while maintaining range size $3$ and unit variance, Lemma 9 fails — i.e., the all-ones vector is no longer the worst case.

nodes.name: Strict improvement for fixed $d$
nodes.statement: Since $\mathbb{E}[Y_1^{2\ell}] < \mathbb{E}[T_1^{2\ell}]$ for some $\ell$, both inequalities of Lemma 6 are strict for each fixed $d$, yielding marginally better tail bounds than the spherically symmetric case.

nodes.name: Direct Jensen bound for sign case
nodes.statement: When $Y_i \in \{-1, +1\}$, Jensen's inequality gives $\mathbb{E}[Q^{2k}]$ bounded directly without comparison to $\mathbb{E}[T^{2k}]$, and $Y_i \in \{-1,+1\}$ minimizes $\mathbb{E}[\exp(h Q^2)]$ for all $h$.
